title: Man, 26, dies in gunfight with police in Edmonton
article: Edmonton police were investigating a complaint of a weapon early yesterday morning when officers found themselves in the middle of a gunfight, which ended with one man dead and a junior constable seriously wounded.
Constable Daniel Furman, 26, was shot in the hand, shoulder and chest, but the protective bulletproof vest he was wearing likely saved his life, police said.
"Thankfully, it hit the armour and didn't cause any more serious injuries. Definitely the armour played a huge part in that," police spokeswoman Karen Carlson said.
The suspect, Darren James Cardinal, 26, also was shot several times during the incident and died a few hours later in hospital.

Constable Furman was one of three officers called to a disturbance at a home in the city's north end when somebody walking in the working-class neighbourhood alerted them to a possible gun inside another nearby home, Ms. Carlson said.

When police arrived at the two-level unit at 12838 68th St. at about 12:20 a.m., they found several residents at home. A senior officer went upstairs, while Constable Furman, who has been with the police service for about 21⁄2 years, and another junior officer went down to the basement.
"A few moments after that, gunshots were heard and our members of the police service responded with gunfire aimed at an assailant," Staff Sergeant Gerry Gunn told reporters yesterday.
The assailant was found with a handgun, but police couldn't say whether it was a registered or illegal weapon.
Constable Furman underwent lengthy surgery and was in serious but stable condition yesterday. He is expected to recover.
Police Chief Mike Boyd was at the hospital soon after the shooting and also visited with the wounded officer's parents. Constable Furman's brother also is a member of the police service.
